questions: Did s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall below the iteration 4 values of 1.4 and 1.95 per run? Report the count per track.
Did max_error on s-bend and slalom fall below 0.06 m, and how many runs still ended off-track? Report off-track counts per track.
Did the oval finish rate stay at or above 16/20 with completion_time near 1.8 s, or did the narrower track make the oval worse?
Did oval steering_oscillation rise above the 0.28 seen in iteration 4? If so, is it a weight problem for the controller rather than a geometry one?
If line-loss is still above 1.0 with wheel_track 0.10, is the next lever a further narrowing to 0.09 m, or should the controller's weights change first?

intent: Keep the iteration 4 geometry (y = 0.07 m, ±0.03 m span at 0.015 m spacing, 0.012 m footprint, mass 0.7 kg, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body unchanged) and narrow wheel_track from 0.11 to 0.10 m to add turn authority on the s-bend and slalom, where line-loss is still 1.4 to 1.95 per run and runs exit with max_error near 0.063 m. Success means s-bend and slalom line-loss falls toward 1.0 or below, max_error drops under 0.06 m, and the oval finish rate holds at 16/20 or better.
learning: Iteration 4 showed that moving the sensor row forward to y = 0.07 m improved the oval (13/20 to 16/20 finishes) but left the sharp tracks unchanged, with line-loss at 1.4 to 1.95 per run. So forward look-ahead is not the gap on s-bend and slalom, and the next test is turn authority through wheel_track alone. If line-loss still does not fall with wheel_track 0.10, the bottleneck is more likely the controller's response on sharp bends than any remaining geometry lever.
rationale: Iteration 4 (y = 0.07 m) is the new best at 364.1, up from 337.5. Oval finishes rose from 13/20 to 16/20, with max_error down to 0.037 m and oval completion time unchanged at 1.82 s. The sharp tracks did not improve. s-bend line-loss is 1.4 per run and slalom rose to 1.95 (from 1.1), with max_error still 0.063 to 0.064 m and 0/20 finishes on both. My own decision rule for this race said that if line-loss stays at about 1.1 or more with max_error near 0.06 m, forward position is not the gap and the next lever is turn authority. That condition holds on the sharp tracks, so forward position is no longer the limiting geometry. Span and footprint were already ruled out by iterations 2 and 3. Speed is not limiting. The remaining untested geometry lever is wheel_track, which sets turn rate per unit of wheel PWM difference. I keep y = 0.07 m because it helped the oval, and I narrow wheel_track from 0.11 to 0.10 m, the next step my plan named, changing nothing else. The Integrator's controller stays as is, so the race isolates turn authority. Expected result: s-bend and slalom line-loss falls toward 1.0 or below and max_error drops under 0.06 m, with at least some sharp-track finishes. Risk: a narrower track may increase oval steering_oscillation (0.28 now), which would be a weight question for the Integrator. The Integrator's earlier suggestion of wheel_radius changes is not supported, since speed is not the limit.
